passages.title: A: Glenmore Lakes Campsite
passages.text: Glenmore Lakes Campsite sits beside a large lake at the foot of the mountains, with walking paths leading straight from the gate. Experienced sailors can hire boats and canoes, although we do not offer lessons. Please note that we cannot accept pets. The site is next to the main road, so it is easy to reach by car.

passages.title: B: Sandy Bay Holiday Park
passages.text: Sandy Bay Holiday Park is right next to a beach where the water stays shallow a long way out, and lifeguards are on duty all summer. Every caravan has its own kitchen, so you can cook whenever you like. If the weather turns bad, the indoor play centre offers games, crafts and films for under-tens.

passages.title: C: The Seacliff Hotel
passages.text: The Seacliff Hotel offers comfortable rooms with sea views and a spa with a pool, sauna and massages. Guests do not need a car: our free minibus meets every train at the station. From the hotel's own harbour, boat trips leave twice a day to watch the dolphins and seals that live along this part of the coast.

passages.title: D: Valmora Old Town
passages.text: Valmora's old town really comes alive after dark, when its bars and squares fill with live music until the early hours. Backpackers love the Blue Door Hostel, where a bed costs just £15 a night. Don't leave without booking an evening at the Valmora Kitchen School, where local chefs show small groups how to make the region's famous dishes.

passages.title: E: The Hilltop Hotel
passages.text: The Hilltop Hotel is a short walk from a sandy beach that is perfect for young children. All meals are served in our restaurant, as rooms do not have kitchens, and there is an outdoor kids' club every morning. Adults can relax in our new spa. The nearest railway station is 20 kilometres away, so guests will need a car.

passages.title: F: The Isle of Carra
passages.text: No cars are allowed on the Isle of Carra, so the only sounds you will hear are birds and the sea. Paths lead over the hills to the island's highest point, with wonderful views. The small museum by the harbour tells the story of the families who have lived here for over a thousand years. Rooms are available at two guesthouses.

passages.title: G: Brenton Harbour Hostel
passages.text: Brenton Harbour Hostel has beds from £16 a night and a large kitchen for guests. On Tuesdays and Fridays our cook runs a cookery class where you can learn to make fresh pasta. Brenton is a peaceful fishing town, so don't expect much nightlife – most cafés and restaurants close by ten o'clock.

passages.title: H: Windy Point Campsite
passages.text: Windy Point Campsite is on a wide, open beach that is ideal for water sports. Our instructors give sailing and windsurfing lessons for complete beginners, and all equipment is provided. Pitch your tent just behind the dunes. Dogs are very welcome, and there is a special area of beach where they can run freely.

questions.question: Lucy and her husband want a beach holiday with their two children, aged four and six. They want a beach where it is safe for small children to swim, and they would like to cook their own meals. They also need something for the children to do indoors if it rains.
questions.explanation: Sandy Bay has a beach 'where the water stays shallow a long way out' with lifeguards, 'every caravan has its own kitchen', and 'if the weather turns bad, the indoor play centre offers games, crafts and films for under-tens'. The Hilltop Hotel also has a beach 'perfect for young children', but 'rooms do not have kitchens' and its kids' club is outdoors.

questions.question: Tom wants a quiet holiday away from traffic, where he can spend his days walking in the hills. He is also interested in history and would like to find out about the people who have lived in the area.
questions.explanation: On the Isle of Carra 'no cars are allowed', 'paths lead over the hills', and the museum 'tells the story of the families who have lived here for over a thousand years'. Glenmore Lakes also has walking paths, but it is 'next to the main road' and says nothing about history.

questions.question: Priya and her friend are students with very little money. They enjoy going out to hear live music at night, and they would like to learn how to cook some local food during their holiday.
questions.explanation: In Valmora the bars and squares 'fill with live music until the early hours', a hostel bed 'costs just £15 a night', and at the Kitchen School 'local chefs show small groups how to make the region's famous dishes'. Brenton Harbour Hostel is also cheap and has a cookery class, but it warns 'don't expect much nightlife'.

questions.question: Mr and Mrs Gordon are retired and do not want to drive on holiday. They would like to stay in a comfortable hotel where they can relax in a spa, and they want to go out on the water to see wildlife.
questions.explanation: The Seacliff Hotel has 'comfortable rooms' and a spa, 'guests do not need a car' because a free minibus meets every train, and 'boat trips leave twice a day to watch the dolphins and seals'. The Hilltop Hotel also has a spa, but 'guests will need a car' and it offers no boat trips.

questions.question: Daniel has never tried water sports before and would like to have lessons in sailing or windsurfing. He wants to go camping and take his dog with him.
questions.explanation: Windy Point Campsite gives 'sailing and windsurfing lessons for complete beginners', you can 'pitch your tent', and 'dogs are very welcome'. Glenmore Lakes is also a campsite with boats, but only 'experienced sailors can hire boats', 'we do not offer lessons' and 'we cannot accept pets'.
